evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: abstract DomainError with ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError subclasses. These are the only errors the module throws.
src/domain/project.ts: createProject throws ValidationError('Project name must not be empty'). ProjectRepository is the port for this entity.
src/domain/user.ts: createUser throws ValidationError('User name must not be empty'). UserRepository has the same shape as ProjectRepository.

src/domain/task.ts: TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus and isTaskStatus define the status values in one place. Task.markDone throws ConflictError and is the only place the completion rule lives. TaskRepository/TaskFilter is the port for this entity.
The trim-and-non-empty check in createProject, createUser and the Task constructor applies to a different entity field each time. It is not one shared invariant written out in several places.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module covers one concern: the core domain model of a project/task/user tracker. That means the entities, the validation rules that come with them, the repository ports and a shared error hierarchy. Every entity file uses the same layout: an entity type, a constructor or factory that checks its own invariants, and a repository interface. All of them throw the module's own DomainError subclasses from errors.ts and never a raw Error, so they stay inside the module's abstractions. Each rule lives in one place. Task status values are defined only in TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus and isTaskStatus. The completion rule (a task can't be marked done twice) is only in Task.markDone. The "trim, then reject empty" check shows up in createProject, createUser and the Task constructor, but each copy guards a different field on a different entity and has its own message. That is a small repeated pattern, not one shared invariant copied around. The modelling style is mixed: Task is a mutable class because it has state changes, while Project and User are readonly interfaces built by factory functions. That fits their behaviour and doesn't break any boundary. Nothing in the unit bypasses its own abstractions or mixes in unrelated concerns.
